title: Evaluating LLMs for Combinatorial Optimization: One-Phase and Two-Phase Heuristics for 2D Bin-Packing
venue: NeurIPS Workshop on Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle: Benchmarks, Emergent Abilities, and Scaling

publication.venue: NeurIPS Workshop on Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle: Benchmarks, Emergent Abilities, and Scaling

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-generated Python heuristics for two-dimensional bin packing
mechanism.populationDetail: High-performing scripts are grouped by logic and performance into islands after each scoring round; independent island-local breeding or migration is not specified.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Top-performing islands supply examples, but no separately maintained elite archive or archive admission rule is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper reports batches of scripts over six rounds without a precise old-to-new population survivor rule.
mechanism.generationDetail: The model writes a new heuristic function from the task specification and, after round one, three example scripts; no one script is designated as editable parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Performance scores determine which islands/examples enter later prompts; explicit numeric score or validator-error text in the prompt is not shown.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The three selected scripts are in-context examples, not identified as true edited parents; Section 3 loosely calls them top performers while Appendix B.10 states random selection within the top three islands.

provenance.citationWarning: Currently cited only in the application section. Island persistence, archive/replacement rule and the exact use of evaluator metrics in prompts are underspecified; the specific appendix says random example selection within top three islands. Treat these three scripts as contextual references, not proven true parents.
